territorial_scope.description: Applies to computer data centers located in Arizona, as the facility is defined by reference to parcels of land in this state.

evidence.quote: means one or more parcels of land in this state

summary.short: Arizona statute allowing tax relief (deductions on sales, use and related transactions in computer data center equipment) for owners, operators and qualified colocation tenants of data centers certified by the state authority, from August 31, 2013, subject to investment thresholds and a qualification period.
summary.long: From August 31, 2013, the owner or operator of a computer data center certified by the state authority, and its qualified colocation tenants, may claim tax relief. The relief is the deduction of gross proceeds or gross income from sales, use, installation, assembly, repair or maintenance of computer data center equipment under listed sections of Title 42. Applicants file a form with the authority, which must approve or deny within sixty days or the application is deemed approved; the certification then runs for a qualification period of ten full calendar years, or twenty for sustainable redevelopment projects. A new data center must invest at least $25,000,000 (county population of 800,000 or fewer) or $50,000,000 (larger counties) within five years of certification, with notice to the authority and records kept until the requirement is met; an existing data center needs $250,000,000 invested in the 72 months before September 1, 2013. Owners must list qualified colocation tenants. The center may not generate electricity for resale or sell electricity outside the center. The authority revokes certification for non-compliance with the investment requirements (permitting recapture of relief by the department of revenue) or for violation of the electricity restriction. Proprietary business information in applications is confidential.

"Computer data center" means all or part of a facility that may be composed of multiple businesses or owners, that is or will be predominantly used to house working servers

"Computer data center equipment" means equipment that is used to outfit, operate or benefit a computer data center and component parts, installations, refreshments, replacements and upgrades to this equipment
"Contributing qualified colocation tenant" means a qualified colocation tenant that is an operator or that had its anticipated investment included in an application for certification

"Existing building" means any existing vertical building improvement located at a facility used for commercial purposes at the time of its acquisition by an owner, but not including single family residential structures, barns or other agricultural structures.
"Existing computer data center" means a computer data center that is certified under subsection E, paragraph 2 of this section.
"Facility" means one or more parcels of land in this state and any structures and personal property contained on the land.
"Investment" means all monies spent to acquire a facility regardless of prior use and all monies spent to construct or expand a computer data center

"Modular data center" means a portable system of information technology, climate control, energy supply and energy distribution machinery, equipment and related tangible personal property contained in an intermodal freight container or similar structure.
"New computer data center" means a computer data center that is certified under subsection E, paragraph 1 of this section.
"Operator" means any individual or entity that operates a computer data center as an operator or lessor or pursuant to a contract with an owner or lessor.
With respect to the owner or operator of a computer data center, a period of time beginning on the effective date of the computer data center's certification
"Qualified colocation tenant" means an entity that contracts with the owner, the operator or another qualified colocation tenant of a computer data center that is certified pursuant to this section
"Sustainable redevelopment project" means a computer data center that satisfies the requirements in subsection E of this section and is either:
"Tax relief" means the deductions of the gross proceeds of sale or gross income from the sale, use, installation, assembly, repair or maintenance of computer data center equipment

obligations.summary: To qualify for tax relief, the owner or operator must submit an application to the authority on a prescribed form, including the listed information (name and contact details, site address, and affirmations tied to subsection E certification requirements).

evidence.quote: the owner or operator shall submit to the authority an application on a form prescribed by the authority

obligations.summary: The authority must review a complete application and either issue a written certification or give written reasons for denial; failure to act within sixty days is deemed approval, and written certification must follow within fourteen days. The authority must send a copy of the certification to the department of revenue.

obligations.summary: The authority may not certify any new computer data center whose application is submitted after December 31, 2033.

evidence.quote: The authority shall not certify any new computer data center that submits an application to the authority after December 31, 2033.

obligations.summary: A computer data center must meet one of two investment requirements, counting combined investment of the owner, operator and qualified colocation tenants: a minimum new investment within five years of certification (paragraph 1, with county population-based amounts), or a qualifying investment in the seventy-two months before September 1, 2013 (paragraph 2).

obligations.summary: If the authority determines non-compliance with the E(1) requirements or a violation of subsection M, it must revoke the certification (with automatic termination of qualification periods). Appeals of revocation go under chapter 6, article 10 of title 41. The department of revenue may recapture tax relief in the first case; in the subsection M violation case it may not recapture relief received before revocation.
